preview.sourceTitle: Refactor auth middleware and session invalidation
preview.sourceDescription: Replace token-based auth. Revoked access can remain valid until the token expires.
preview.why: Some removed accounts can retain access for too long. This change makes that access immediately revocable.
preview.impact: No visible change to day-to-day use. The work mainly improves security.

faq.q1: Does Diaphane replace my project tracker?
faq.a1: No. Your board remains where you manage the project. Diaphane is designed to connect to different project trackers; GitHub Projects is the first integration available.
faq.q2: What does Diaphane do with my documents?
faq.a2: Diaphane analyzes their content, sorts it into the project's topics, structures it into useful sections, then explains it in plain language. You can approve, reject, or refile every section before publishing.
faq.q3: What exactly can my client see?
faq.a3: A read-only view of their project: current task, progress, team, approved documentation, and meeting information when provided.
faq.q4: How do I invite my client?
faq.a4: Create an invitation inside the project, then share the secure link generated by Diaphane. The client uses it to create or join their account.
faq.a5: Diaphane instructs the AI to work only from the available sources. You stay in control: document sections are never published without your approval.
faq.a6: Every session is authenticated and tied to one user. Clients can only access projects they have been invited to.
faq.a7: Diaphane is in launch phase. Pricing will be announced soon; you can already create an account and a first project.

Pipeline.title: Project documentation
Pipeline.description: Your documents become documentation your client can read. Diaphane writes it, you approve what is true. Four steps, in order.
Pipeline.loadError: This project's documentation could not be loaded.

Steps.title1: What Diaphane took from your documents
Steps.purpose1: Everything your documents say, gathered in one place and tied back to where it came from. This is the raw material — not what your client reads.
Steps.title2: The sections your client will read
Steps.purpose2: You name a section, say what it should cover, and Diaphane writes it from what your documents say. Nothing is published without your approval.
Steps.purpose3: The final result. It changes only when you approve a section — never halfway.

Sections.emptyDescription: A section is a heading your client will read. You choose its name, its tone, and what Diaphane should look for in your documents.

Editor.nameHint: This is the heading your client reads, exactly as you write it.
Editor.instructionsHint: The field that matters most. The more precise you are, the better the writing.

Editor.staleError: This section changed while you were editing it. Reopen it to start from the current version.
Editor.suggestion_overview_instructions: What the client asked for, why, and what the project must produce. The goals, the scope, and the constraints around them.
Editor.suggestion_howItWorks_instructions: The technical choices and the reasons behind them, explained without jargon. What the product does, how the pieces fit, and what that means for the user.
Editor.suggestion_planning_instructions: The dates, the deadlines, the planned deliveries and the order they arrive in. What is confirmed, and what still needs confirming.
Editor.suggestion_audit_instructions: What the existing system reveals: what works, what causes trouble, the risks found, and the recommendations that follow.
